excerpt: Spoken Dialogue Models (SDMs) typically share a speech-token space for generation and synthesis, leading to long autoregressive sequences and costly inference. Lower-rate speech tokenizers shorten sequences but may introduce compression-quality trade-offs and costly replacement without breaking this coupling. To address this limitation, we propose CoSTA, a compatibility-preserving post-hoc framework that decouples generation and synthesis token spaces while retaining the original speech tokenizer and decoder. ai.summary: CoSTA is a post‑hoc framework that decouples generation and synthesis token spaces in spoken dialogue models, preserving compatibility while reducing token length for faster inference.
ai.why: Allows developers to improve spoken dialogue system efficiency without retraining the entire model.

title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding

However, existing proactive paradigms typically assume that the information required to answer a query is complete, leaving models to only wait or answer. In the real world, however, information is often incomplete due to uncertainty from either the video or the user. In proactive paradigms, such uncertainty can cause the model to wait forever or generate highly hallucinatory responses. We…

excerpt: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. First, we prove a Platonic Representation Theorem: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) trained separately on any number of modalities learn the same representation up to one rotation whenever their positive pairs are two observations of one scene--good views--and their misalignment is bounded otherwise. title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
excerpt: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image.
